articles.title: Las lecciones para el Clásico
articles.standfirst: París demuestra que el equipo azulgrana debe mejorar en varios aspectos
articles.summary: París demuestra que el equipo azulgrana debe mejorar en varios aspectos
articles.body: En Can Barça todos sabían que el partido frente al PSG iba a ser muy complicado. Enfrente tenían al actual campeón de Europa, un equipo con un enorme potencial ofensivo, como volvió a demostrar en esta ocasión al marcar cuatro goles. Los de Luis Enrique fueron superiores a su rival, que perdió por primera vez esta temporada. Y lo hicieron porque cometieron muchos errores en diferentes fases del partido. Es un encuentro del que los azulgranas podrán aprender mucho de cara al futuro y, sobre todo, para el choque del próximo domingo frente al Real Madrid. Hubo varios motivos por los que el Barcelona perdió en el Parque de los Príncipes y de los que debe extraer conclusiones en los próximos días. Así lo manifestaron tanto el entrenador como los jugadores que hablaron al finalizar el encuentro. «Hemos tenido ocasiones que tenemos que materializar. Hay que jugar con más calma. Hay que vigilar las distancias entre los jugadores. Lo tenemos que hacer mejor», dijo Hansi Flick. Uno de los factores clave de la derrota fueron las pérdidas de balón de los azulgranas. En los primeros cinco minutos, Pedri perdió tres balones que se tradujeron en claras ocasiones para el PSG. Tras una de esas pérdidas, Kvaratskhelia estrelló el balón en el palo y Joan García tuvo que realizar sus dos primeras paradas de la noche. Dos goles llegaron tras sendas pérdidas de balón en la medular, una de ellas de Lamine Yamal. Si el Barcelona quiere proclamarse campeón de Europa, no puede permitirse perder tantos balones, y menos aún en esa zona del campo. El PSG supo aprovechar estos errores y generar numerosas ocasiones. Los de Luis Enrique remataron 15 veces entre los tres palos ante el conjunto azulgrana. Ningún rival había alcanzado esta cifra frente al Barça en la última década. El equipo de Flick tiene que cerrar mejor los espacios y dificultar el camino hacia su área. En Europa hay que ser efectivo. El Barcelona creó numerosas ocasiones a lo largo del partido, demostrando también que es muy peligroso en ataque, pero los de Flick erraron en la puntería. Lamine, Raphinha y Gordon no tuvieron su noche, a pesar de que el primero marcó un golazo. Los jugadores de Flick realizaron 18 remates en total, pero solo cinco fueron entre los tres palos. El Barça no supo imponer en muchos momentos el ritmo de partido que más le convenía. En lugar de controlar el encuentro, este se convirtió en un intercambio de golpes en el que los franceses salieron victoriosos. Es cierto que hubo fases de la segunda parte en las que los azulgranas sí lograron dominar y tuvieron más posesión que su rival. Eso les permitió empatar el partido, pero, a partir de ahí, les faltó mantener el control. En este sentido, el factor Rodri es fundamental. Es cierto que Flick tiene que dosificar a sus jugadores, pero cuesta entender que el centrocampista fuera el sacrificado en un partido tan importante como el del PSG. Aunque el domingo espere el Real Madrid, la presencia del exganador del Balón de Oro se antoja fundamental. Se le echó de menos en la primera parte, en la que Pedri no fue capaz de imponer el ritmo que necesitaba el equipo. Cuando Rodri saltó al campo en la segunda mitad, junto a Gavi, ninguno de los dos logró convertirse en el revulsivo que necesitaba el conjunto azulgrana. Otro factor que hay que tener en cuenta es la defensa a balón parado. El Barça encajó un gol de córner y no pudo evitar el certero cabezazo de Lucas Hernández. El PSG supo culminar una buena acción de estrategia que se convirtió en el 2-1 para los franceses. El Barcelona demostró que tiene potencial para competir contra los mejores equipos de Europa, pero debe mejorar estos aspectos defensivos si realmente quiere aspirar a conquistar la Champions. La pasada temporada, su rendimiento defensivo fue clave para explicar por qué el equipo azulgrana no llegó más lejos en esta competición.

articles.title: Xavi Espart, Gerard Martin react after PSG 4-2 Barcelona: ‘The defeat won’t affect El Clasico’
articles.summary: Barcelona’s 2-4 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain offered little comfort on the scoreboard, but the performances of Xavi Espart and Gerard Martin provided Hansi...
articles.body:
Barcelona's 2-4 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain offered little comfort on the scoreboard, but the performances of Xavi Espart and Gerard Martin provided Hansi Flick with reasons for optimism ahead of Sunday's El Clasico against Real Madrid.

The two young players featured prominently in a demanding European encounter, with Espart scoring his first Champions League goal and Martin playing despite carrying a niggle.

Their post-match reflections shared a common theme: Barcelona must learn from the defeat without allowing it to undermine their confidence before facing their biggest domestic rivals.

Espart celebrates milestone despite Barcelona defeat

Espart emerged as one of Barcelona's standout performers against PSG, capping an impressive display with a goal.

However, the right-back made it clear that individual achievements carried less weight than the team's result.

"We knew it was a very demanding match; they have a great team, but we have to take the positives from it.

"We gave 100% and small details decided the match, and it's good for us to see the areas we need to improve and continue to grow."

The teenager acknowledged the mixed emotions surrounding his first goal in the Champions League, particularly given Barcelona's inability to secure a positive result.

"It's a bit bittersweet, because the team's victory comes first, but I'm very happy with my first Champions League goal.

"Ultimately, it's bittersweet because I would have liked to come away with the win, but I'll take the positives from what I've done and what the team has done, and we're focused on Sunday."

Gerard Martin reveals he played through a niggle

Martin also reflected on the physical demands of the contest, confirming that he had been carrying a minor problem before taking part.

The defender explained that players regularly have to manage discomfort when important fixtures arrive.

"Ultimately, all players play a few matches whilst carrying niggles, and in a match like this you do everything you can to play ."

Assessing the performance, Martin pointed to the intensity of both teams' pressing and the importance of taking chances when opportunities arise.

"It was a very demanding match; both sides had their moments, because we both pressed high up the pitch and when the pressure eased there were plenty of spaces for us and for them.

"In the end, it comes down to the finer details – making the most of our chances. We'll have to correct what we did wrong, but it's only October and we've got plenty of room for improvement."

Barcelona youngsters turn attention towards El Clasico

Despite the European setback, Martin insisted that the result would not damage Barcelona's confidence ahead of their meeting with Real Madrid.

He believes the team can take pride in competing at a high level while addressing the details that went against them.

"It won't affect us, because we've competed at the highest level and put in a great performance – apart from those small details that cost us a few goals – but we can hold our heads high, and we've got El Clasico this weekend, which we'll go out to win," he concluded.

articles.title: Bayern Munich legend highlights importance of Vincent Kompany
articles.summary: FC Bayern could be without its main man vs. Arsenal.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich has a massive Champions League test against Arsenal tomorrow, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge knows exactly what is at stake. The former Bayern Munich CEO also provided a concerning update on Vincent Kompany, whose illness could prevent him from taking his place on the touchline.

"It's a classic. During my time as CEO, we played against them almost every year—and won almost every year. Last year, however, we lost 3-1, and that defeat was deserved. We need to make sure we win now after needlessly throwing away two points last week, but it won't be easy," Rummenigge said (as captured by Tz's Vinzent Tschirpke via @iMiaSanMia ).

Bayern Munich cannot afford another frustrating result after dropping points last week. Arsenal will present a formidable challenge, particularly with Michael Olise suspended, leaving Kompany with another significant selection headache ahead of a match that could prove crucial to Bayern's European ambitions.

However, the bigger concern might be whether Kompany can even lead his team from the sidelines.

"We're missing one of our best players in Michael Olise. We also need to see whether the coach will be able to take his place on the bench. He's been suffering from a virus since Saturday. Yesterday morning, he seemed to be feeling better, but his condition deteriorated somewhat as the day went on. Perhaps it would be better for him to take the time to recover fully. He is the driving force behind everything we do—and the architect of the success we've enjoyed so far," said Rummenigge.

Rummenigge's praise highlights just how important Kompany has become to Bayern Munich's resurgence. Still, with Arsenal waiting and Olise unavailable, Bayern may have to navigate its biggest test of the season without two of its most influential figures.

If Kompany cannot recover in time, his players will need to demonstrate that the mentality and tactical identity he has instilled in this team can withstand adversity. Bayern has the quality to beat Arsenal, but it will need a complete performance to leave London with the result it wants.

articles.title: Ngumoha Takes Centre Stage as Liverpool Survive Villarreal Scare
articles.summary: Liverpool 4–3 Villarreal – Champions League Post-Match ReportBy Steven SmithAfter a heartening victory away to Brentford in the Premier League, Liverpool ret...
articles.body:
Liverpool 4–3 Villarreal – Champions League Post-Match Report

After a heartening victory away to Brentford in the Premier League, Liverpool returned to Anfield for a Champions League encounter against Villarreal. The Reds were looking to build on their European thrashing of LASK, but what followed was a chaotic seven-goal thriller that tested the team's character, exposed familiar defensive concerns and ultimately showcased the extraordinary potential of Rio Ngumoha.

Andoni Iraola's side recovered from a dreadful opening half-hour to turn the game around, with Alexis Mac Allister scoring twice and Florian Wirtz adding a fourth. However, conceding three goals and allowing Villarreal to threaten throughout meant this was far from a complete performance.

Liverpool 0–1 Villarreal – Georges Mikautadze – 4'

Liverpool 0–2 Villarreal – Sergi Cardona (Nathan-Dylan Saliba) – 29'

Liverpool 1–2 Villarreal – Alexis Mac Allister (Kostas Tsimikas) – 36'

Liverpool 2–2 Villarreal – Ronald Araújo (Rio Ngumoha) – 45+2'

Liverpool 3–2 Villarreal – Alexis Mac Allister (Rio Ngumoha) – 65'

Liverpool 4–2 Villarreal – Florian Wirtz (Cody Gakpo) – 69'

Possession – Liverpool 53% | Villarreal 47%

Total Shots – Liverpool 21 | Villarreal 14

Shots on Target – Liverpool 7 | Villarreal 5

Liverpool could hardly have made a worse start. Just four minutes into the contest, Georges Mikautadze put Villarreal ahead, leaving the home side chasing the game before they had properly settled. The early goal exposed Liverpool's lack of defensive organisation, and the Reds struggled to establish control in the opening stages.

Things deteriorated further in the 29th minute when Sergi Cardona doubled Villarreal's advantage, assisted by Nathan-Dylan Saliba. At 2–0 down, Liverpool looked vulnerable, short of confidence and unable to cope with the visitors' movement. For the opening half-hour, this was a deeply concerning performance from Iraola's side.

Yet Rio Ngumoha was one of the few players offering genuine hope. The teenage winger repeatedly looked to take defenders on, attack space and create something from nothing. While his teammates struggled to find their rhythm, he played with the confidence and directness Liverpool desperately needed.

The turning point arrived in the 36th minute. Kostas Tsimikas supplied the assist for Alexis Mac Allister, whose goal brought Liverpool back into the contest. It was a much-needed response, giving Anfield something to believe in and allowing the home side to finish the half with greater purpose.

Then came the equaliser in stoppage time. Ngumoha delivered another decisive contribution, setting up Ronald Araújo to make it 2–2 in the 45th minute plus added time. From looking completely out of the game, Liverpool had dragged themselves level before the interval.

It was a remarkable turnaround, although the defensive performance remained a major concern. Liverpool had shown their attacking quality, but they needed a far more controlled second half if they were to complete the comeback.

Liverpool emerged with renewed belief, and the introduction of Florian Wirtz for Araújo at half-time added another creative dimension to the attack. The Reds began to move the ball with greater purpose, while Mac Allister increasingly took control of the midfield.

Ngumoha continued to be the outstanding attacking threat. His direct running and ability to beat defenders repeatedly unsettled Villarreal, and in the 65th minute he produced another important contribution. The winger supplied the assist for Mac Allister's second goal, completing the turnaround and putting Liverpool 3–2 ahead.

Mac Allister's brace was a reward for his improved influence as the game progressed. After a difficult opening period for the team, the Argentine grew into the contest and demonstrated his quality in front of goal. His ability to combine midfield control with decisive attacking contributions proved crucial.

Four minutes later, Liverpool extended their lead. Cody Gakpo provided the assist for Wirtz, who finished to make it 4–2 in the 69th minute. Anfield had witnessed a remarkable transformation, with Liverpool now seemingly in control after their disastrous start.

However, the Reds could not entirely remove the tension. Villarreal continued to threaten, and Liverpool's defensive vulnerabilities remained evident. The visitors eventually found a third goal, ensuring a nervy conclusion and reminding Iraola that his side still have plenty to improve despite their attacking brilliance.

Ngumoha was withdrawn in the 73rd minute, with Bradley Barcola introduced, while Joe Gomez replaced Jacquet. Isak had already come on for Koumas in the 67th minute, and James McConnell later replaced Nyoni. The changes helped Liverpool manage the closing stages, but the contest remained uncomfortable until the final whistle.

The statistics underline Liverpool's attacking superiority, with 21 shots and an expected-goals figure of 2.37 compared with Villarreal's 14 shots and 1.58 xG. Nevertheless, conceding three goals at home will concern the coaching staff, particularly after the defensive issues that surfaced against LASK.

This was an extraordinary Champions League night at Anfield, but one that offered both encouragement and warning signs. Liverpool showed tremendous character to recover from two goals down, and their attacking players delivered when it mattered. Mac Allister's brace and Wirtz's contribution were important, but Ngumoha was the defining figure of the evening.

The teenage winger was sensational, producing two assists and repeatedly taking responsibility when Liverpool needed inspiration. His performance demonstrated why he is such an exciting prospect, particularly in his developing role on the right wing. If he continues to combine that directness with end product, he could become a major weapon for Iraola.

Jérémy Jacquet was again a reassuring presence at the back, while Mac Allister's second-half display showed his importance to the side. However, the opening 30 minutes were unacceptable, and the defensive errors that allowed Villarreal to score three times cannot be overlooked.

Liverpool's attacking quality ultimately carried them through, but Iraola will know that better-organised opponents could punish the same mistakes more severely. The Reds have now demonstrated that they can fight back from adversity, but the next step is avoiding the need for such dramatic recoveries in the first place.

My pre-match prediction was Liverpool 3–1 Villarreal. The Reds scored four, conceded three and secured the victory, but the scoreline tells only part of the story. It was an entertaining European comeback, powered by Ngumoha's brilliance, yet there is plenty for Liverpool to address before their next test.

articles.title: Arteta backs 'best in the world' praise for 'remarkable' Gabriel-Konsa partnership
articles.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has backed the assessment that Gabriel Maghalaes and Ezri Konsa are the best centre-back partnership in world football right now...
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has backed the assessment that Gabriel Maghalaes and Ezri Konsa are the best centre-back partnership in world football right now.

Oliver Glasner made that statement after his Nottingham Forest side were frustrated by Arsenal's defensive duo at the weekend, during the Gunners' 1-0 win at the City Ground.

Konsa has made an immediate impression since his arrival from Aston Villa in the summer, forming a fine understanding with Gabriel in the absence of William Saliba.

Saliba's spell out with a back issue sparked fears in the summer, but Arsenal have recorded four clean sheets in seven Premier League games.

Arteta was asked about the new-look pair in central defence and admitted it is 'remarkable' how soon the two have formed an understanding.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Bayern Munich in the Champions League tonight, Arteta said: "That's a great opinion! For me, my players are the best in the world, and I think the partnership that they have developed in such a short period of time is remarkable.

"Credit to both of them, credit to the rest of the team as well. But I think on Sunday, both of them, specifically in key moments, they were exceptional."

Arsenal's new defensive pairing will face a formidable test tonight, against the German champions in Munich. Harry Kane will lead the line for Bayern Munich, with the 33-year-old a Ballon d'Or frontrunner after scoring 61 goals last season.

Asked if Kane represents the ultimate test for Gabriel and Konsa, Arteta added: Well they get tested a lot in the Premier League certainly, and they have already done in the Champions League . But I think what Harry's doing, and has done in the last few years, is just something else, another level. That's what we have to face tomorrow."

articles.title: Fulham put on best attacking display against Hull - now they need to convert chances
articles.summary: Fulham finally got their win over Hull but now it is up to the Cottagers to improve their finishing and get themselves up the table.
articles.body:
Tom Masters explains that Fulham need to score more goals.

Fulham may have only beaten Hull 1-0 on Saturday but anyone watching will know just how impressive a performance it was.

Under immense pressure, having failed to win in the Premier League in their first six games and after throwing away five points in two matches from winning positions, Fulham were expected to struggle against Hull.

But they did anything but that, completely dominating possession from the outset and having big chances from the third minute onwards.

Really, Fulham will feel as though they should have come away with a much more routine win than they did.

And that is for one reason and one reason only - it was quite simply their best attacking performance of the season so far.

Alex Iwobi scored one; he could have had a hat-trick. Calvin Bassey had a good chance; Josh King had one difficult chance and one that he simply has to score; Gonzalo Garcia absolutely has to bury his header late on.

From that alone, 4-0 does not feel like an exaggeration.

Hull offered nothing and that is something that Fulham must take credit for, because on this occasion, as there had been against Ipswich the week before and arguably also against Manchester United , there was no sitting back when scoring first.

Fulham kept on attacking, kept on creating good opportunities, and absolutely dominated possession.

But I think I can speak for pretty much all Fulham fans when I say that when Ryan Sessegnon was sent off in stoppage time, there was a major sense of here we go again.

Thankfully, this time it was not and Fulham fans were able to breathe a big sigh of relief at Craven Cottage.

Now, after reflecting, Fulham's shape for this match was the best and most balanced it has been.

The midfield pairing of Sander Berge and Shea Charles are forming a good relationship, which is a major contributing factor to Fulham's improving defensive stats and, in turn, to them keeping more of the ball.

If you look at a performance like Hull, it seems impossible that Fulham did not rack up an impressive scoreline.

Football is a tricky sport in that there is always something else to go for, something else to target.

Fulham's was to get their first win, now they have done that, it will be to get their next and this time to be more convincing on the scoresheet.

It feels like it is a matter of time until they do so but until they improve on their finishing, there will be more nervy days ahead.

articles.title: Man Utd face massive Champions League fixture chaos as dangerous weather warnings threaten Como clash
articles.summary: Manchester United's continental ambitions have hit a literal roadblock in Italy as severe weather conditions threaten to derail their latest Champions League...
articles.body:
Extreme rainfall puts Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia pitch at risk

Italian authorities have issued an orange weather alert across the Lombardy region, signalling severe and dangerous conditions. Relentless rain began on Tuesday and has battered the area continually, putting the scheduled European fixture in serious jeopardy. According to Press Association's Simon Peach , forecasts predict up to 64mm of rainfall before the scheduled kick-off at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

The downpour has left the playing surface saturated, while the prospect of lightning adds further safety concerns. Match-going supporters face a particularly grim evening, as only one of the stadium's four stands provides a roof. Despite the treacherous forecast, Como officials currently remain optimistic that the pitch will drain sufficiently to avoid a late cancellation.

United face injury crisis against rising Como side

If the match does proceed, United will face a difficult test against an in-form Como team managed by former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas. The Serie A outfit are enjoying an upward trajectory and feature former Red Devils defender Willy Kambwala within their ranks.

The visitors arrived in Italy heavily depleted . Six first-team players missed training on Tuesday, leaving the squad stretched ahead of their third European assignment. Key figures including Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, and Luke Shaw are among the absentees, alongside Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu.

This mounting injury list compounds a dismal campaign for the English giants. Having secured just two victories across all competitions this term, they are currently enduring their worst start to a season in 40 years.

Carrick brushes off weather and pressure concerns

Despite the turbulent conditions both on and off the pitch, United manager Michael Carrick remains completely unfazed by the Italian storms. Addressing the media before the trip, the boss downplayed the impact of the rain on his squad's preparations. "No, nothing immediate from me, we're used to the rain," Carrick stated. "We'll make the most of it!"

Carrick also addressed his job security amid the club's historically poor start. He insisted that he retains the full support of the Old Trafford hierarchy and understands the demands placed upon him. "I don't need any reassurance. It's pretty clear," he explained. "I know the role, I know my responsibilities, I don't need anyone to tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better.

"I know the realities and have no problem with that. I know we got to win football games for everything to flow and fit into place. I feel backed, yeah, why wouldn't I? I have a really good relationship with everyone at the football club. There are no issues on that side."

United currently sit on a knife-edge in their Champions League campaign, having taken three points from their opening two fixtures. Securing a result in Italy - assuming the weather permits - is vital to maintaining momentum in Europe and easing the mounting scrutiny on the coaching staff.

Navigating this fixture with a heavily rotated squad will require immense tactical discipline. If the pitch at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia devolves into a waterlogged battleground, Carrick's depleted side must abandon their usual patterns of play and embrace a gruelling, physical contest to salvage their season.

articles.title: Rio Ngumoha’s daring display helps Liverpool preserve perfect Champions League record
articles.summary: Rio Ngumoha believes his performance in Liverpool's 4-3 win over Villarreal was one of his best for the senior side.Ngumoha starred as Liverpool recovered fr...
articles.body:
Rio Ngumoha believes his performance in Liverpool 's 4-3 win over Villarreal was one of his best for the senior side.

Ngumoha starred as Liverpool recovered from two goals down at Anfield to maintain their 100% record in this season's Champions League league phase.

The 18-year-old set up goals for Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister, becoming the youngest player ever to assist a goal for Liverpool in European competition.

Ngumoha's name was sung loudly by the Liverpool fans on a fine evening for the teenager, who admitted his display was one of his best for the Reds.

"It's up there with one of the best I've played, I think. I enjoyed myself out there. The team helped me as well a lot. I enjoyed today," he told liverpoolfc.com.

Ngumoha played with real confidence against the Spanish side and said he has the belief to take on full-backs whenever in possession. The winger curled a brilliant ball to the far post for Araujo's equaliser, before leaving his man in his wake to tee up Mac Allister.

"Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one-v-one or two-v-one sometimes, by all means I'll do it. I believe in myself to do it. The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless."

Andoni Iraola: "That's the good thing with Rio, he's still 18, he's not the full package."

Andoni Iraola praised the attitude of Ngumoha at full-time and believes there is still so much to come from the youngster.

"I'm happy with his attitude because he's eager to improve the things that we think he needs to improve. He's eager to add more things to his game. He has changed the sides a lot and has played a lot on the right lately. He's feeling so comfortable now and he's adding even some shots with the left [foot] that he hasn't scored but he's getting there, and if he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position.

"That's the good thing with Rio, he's still 18, he's not the full package. He can add things, fortunately for us also, and I hope he continues the same way. It's not going to be always like this, he will have ups and downs in the process, but I'm happy because attitude-wise I'm seeing him in a great place."

articles.title: Lens XI v Club Brugge: Odsonne Edouard to lead the line
articles.summary: RC Lens pay a visit to Belgian neighbours Club Brugge for Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League. The Ligue 1 side needs to bounce back after a deflating ho...
articles.body:
RC Lens pay a visit to Belgian neighbours Club Brugge for Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League. The Ligue 1 side needs to bounce back after a deflating home loss to Sporting CP last week, but they'll be up against a team that secured a prestigious away win over Serie A champions Inter Milan.

Lens head coach Yannick Cahuzac faces a conundrum over his starting XI due to the absences of highly-rated defensive prospect Ismaël Ganiou. L'Equipe predicts that Matthieu Udol – the team's senior left wing-back – will be deployed on the left side of Lens' three-man defense alongside Samson Baidoo and Kyllian Antonio. This would leave West Ham United loanee Jean-Clair Todibo on the bench.

Up front, Abdallah Sima remains on the sidelines. Former Crystal Palace centre-forward Odsonne Edouard, who scored on Saturday for Lens' away won over Troyes, should be given the nod. Franjo Ivanovic and the excellent Florian Thauvin are also expected to start.

Robin Risser; Matthieu Udol, Samson Baidoo, Kyllian Antonio; Michal Skoras, Amadou Haïdara, Michael Cuisance, Saud Abdulhamid; Franjo Ivanovic, Odsonne Edouard, Florian Thauvin. (L'Éq)

articles.title: Michael Carrick rejects claims of a 'toxic culture' at Manchester United, praising togetherness
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has refuted claims of a toxic culture at Manchester United and insists the group are giving 'everything' to turn results around.Manchester Un...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has refuted claims of a toxic culture at Manchester United and insists the group are giving 'everything' to turn results around.

Manchester United have endured a difficult start to the new season and have taken just seven points from seven Premier League games.

Clean sheets have also been an issue, with only one shut-out in 10 games across all competitions, against Azerbaijani outfit Sabah in the Champions League.

United return to European action against Como this evening, amid the backdrop of noise from former manager Erik ten Hag. In a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic this week, Ten Hag discussed his time at Old Trafford, frustrations, and a challenging culture.

The Dutchman claimed the board helped fuel a 'toxic culture' after not backing him over disciplinary matters involving Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho.

"And so, they are continuing the toxic culture; they fuel it, they give the power to the players," Ten Hag said.

"Rashford is an amazing player, if his mindset is right. I always showed my trust in him, played him. But when you show these standards, sometimes you have to make corrections."

Another of the club's former managers, Ruben Amorim, has made similar comments , but Carrick has insisted he has seen no signs of such since his appointment, despite a recent decline in results.

Speaking at his press conference ahead of facing Como in the Champions League tonight, he said: "No, I haven't. Since I came back the players, the staff, they've given us everything that they could give. Yeah, we've had some good performances. We've had some performances that we want to do better, that we can improve on.

"We've made some mistakes. That's football and that's pushing performance. But, I have to say, and I'll kind of repeat what I said the other day, you know, if you haven't got a good group, the type of performance – I'm not talking about the level – but the type of performance that the boys put into the weekend and, showed in Atletico for large parts, I think, and what the feeling that we have, there's a lot of togetherness there.

"There's a lot of will, there's a lot of determination to do better and want to do it for each other, which is important. So, in that regard as the group, I couldn't be happier with the togetherness, for sure."

articles.title: Would Arsenal want Jeremy Doku or Antoine Semenyo? Ex-Gunners star ‘not convinced’ transfer raids will be launched if Man City are stung with FFP relegation
articles.summary: If Manchester City are hit with Financial Fair Play (FFP) sanctions that result in them being relegated out of the Premier League, could Arsenal be tempted t...
articles.body:
Arsenal were linked with Vini Jr & Barcola

Premier League champions from Emirates Stadium were in the market for a left-sided attacker during the summer transfer window. Energetic Greek forward Christos Tzolis was acquired, with Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli moving on.

Interest was shown in more proven performers, with rumours of Real Madrid 'Galactico' Vinicius Junior potentially heading to north London capturing the imagination at one stage. The Brazilian former Ballon d'Or contender eventually signed a new contract at Santiago Bernabeu.

Bradley Barcola was another to register on Arsenal's recruitment radar, as a star for France and back-to-back Champions League winner with Paris Saint-Germain. His valuation crept ever higher, to the point that Liverpool ended up paying £123 million ($165m) for the 24-year-old.

Man City could be relegated into the Championship

Arteta and Co were seemingly reluctant to dig that deep for one player, with the likes of Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke capable of operating on the flanks and providing added creativity.

If the right option were to become available, though, than the Gunners would likely make their move . They will be keeping a close eye on events in Manchester. With 114 charges hanging over City, it has been suggested that a catastrophic points deduction is on the cards .

If Enzo Maresca's side were to tumble out of the top-flight, then a mass exodus of talent is being predicted . That could include ex-Bournemouth flier Semenyo and tricky wideman Doku - who has taken his game to another level in the Premier League over the last couple of seasons.

Would the Gunners be interested in Doku & Semenyo?

The Belgium international would appear to be tailor-made for Arsenal and their attacking needs , but Grimandi is not so sure. The two-time Premier League title winner, who was speaking in association with BetVictor Online Casino - told GOAL when asked about approaches for wingers that City may have to move on: "I'm not convinced to be honest.

"To play the way they want to play, I don't know. I watched the City games and Doku has fantastic ability, pace but Semenyo, I'm not convinced. I don't think they will bring something special.

"[Khvicha] Kvaratskhelia of course will bring something special to Arsenal. I'm not convinced but I think we have quality as well in the young talent at Arsenal. Maybe it's a chance for them to show their ability.

"It's my point of view now. I cannot see Arsenal spending money but maybe they will become free, Doku or Semenyo."

Arsenal focused on the present & battle with Bayern

Others, such as ex-England international Gabriel Agbonlahor, have claimed that Doku would be "perfect" for Arsenal. Paul Scholes is another to have predicted that the Belgian will head for the Emirates if City drop into the Championship.

It remains to be seen whether Arteta shares that opinion and if he is prepared to meet the demands of trophy-chasing rivals. The expectation is that further reinforcements on the left flank will be sought in 2027.

For now, the Gunners are very much focused on the present. They have an epic European tussle with Harry Kane and Bayern Munich to take in on Wednesday, before then playing host to Everton in domestic competition on Saturday.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund finishing woes overshadow latest Champions League victory
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy was only partially satisfied with his team’s 2-1 Champions League victory over Azerbaijani outfit Sabah FK on Tuesd...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy was only partially satisfied with his team's 2-1 Champions League victory over Azerbaijani outfit Sabah FK on Tuesday evening. Despite scoring both goals in the victory, the Guinean international insisted that he and his teammates still have plenty of work to do.

The victory in Baku ended Dortmund's three-match winless streak , which had included draws against Werder Bremen and Union Berlin as well as a disappointing Champions League defeat against Bodø/Glimt . Guirassy opened the scoring in the tenth minute, reacting quickest after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov failed to hold Felix Nmecha's effort.

The hosts equalized through Aden McCarthy shortly before halftime, but Guirassy restored Dortmund's lead in the 53rd minute after connecting with an excellent Joey Veerman delivery. It was the striker's second Champions League brace of the season, following his two goals in Dortmund's opening victory against Villarreal .

Nevertheless, Guirassy told DAZN that he was only "half satisfied" with the team's performance.

Dortmund lament missed opportunities in Baku

Dortmund finished the encounter with 22 shots and approximately 3.7 expected goals. Guirassy alone accounted for eight shots, while strike partner Fábio Silva squandered an excellent early opportunity. The statistics underlined Dortmund's superiority, but the narrow scoreline meant Niko Kovac's side remained vulnerable to a late equalizer.

"We have to kill the game [off]," Veerman remarked when speaking to reporters in the mixed zone. "We have to score a lot more, I think."

Goalkeeper Gregor Kobel agreed that Dortmund had made life unnecessarily difficult for themselves.

"It took a little too long to put the game to bed," Kobel said. "If one scores a few more goals, such a game would be more relaxed. One felt that there was more in that game. It would have done us good to score four or five goals. It would have been easier."

"Of course, I wish a few more goals had gone in up front," Kobel continued. "But I just have to do my job and remain vigilant at the back."

Kovac shared his players' assessment at the post-match press conference.

"The lads could have and definitely should [have] won the game by a larger margin," the BVB head coach said. "Then we wouldn't have had such a nervy finish."

Sporting director Nils-Ole Book also acknowledged that Dortmund had failed to capitalize on several opportunities that would have settled the contest.

"Of course, if we had scored those two decisive goals it would have been different," Book told reporters in the mixed zone. "That definitely sticks out."

Guirassy challenges Dortmund to maintain higher standards

The best players, Guirassy argued, produce dependable performances every week. He emphasized that Dortmund's squad possessed sufficient quality to meet those standards but needed to demonstrate it more regularly. Importantly, Guirassy did not exempt himself from criticism.

"We're top players, so we have to work on that – myself included," the forward explained in his DAZN interview.

His assessment adds another dimension to Dortmund's recent struggles. The Schwarzgelben began the season impressively, but their attacking difficulties against Bodø/Glimt and Union Berlin had already attracted scrutiny before Tuesday's victory.

Kovač's team now return to Bundesliga action against Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday evening.

articles.title: The major flaw in Arsenal’s Champions League blueprint and how Bayern can expose it
articles.summary: Vincent Kompany, who was, like Mikel Arteta, one of Pep Guardiola’s lieutenants, is committed to a cavalier approach, writes Richard Jolly, which could expos...
articles.body:
The purists against the puritans? The cavaliers against the cautious? It could seem so. Bayern Munich and Arsenal share a status as champions of their country and an ambition to be champions of Europe. Their managers were two of Pep Guardiola's lieutenants, as his captain and assistant respectively at Manchester City. Some may say they learnt different lessons.

Arsenal go to the Allianz Arena after a win at Nottingham Forest in which they had a lone shot on target . Bayern had 17 in their weekend win over RB Leipzig and, while it is both lazy and easy to dismiss their domestic opposition as relative minnows, the reality is they walloped the team who finished third in the Bundesliga last year. Bayern have six goals in their last match, Arsenal six in their last four.

The counter-argument, of course, is that Arsenal have the best defence in Europe, the team that only conceded seven goals in 15 Champions League games last season, the only side to start the current campaign with consecutive clean sheets. By way of comparison, Bayern were breached three times by the Norwegian newcomers Viking last week.

Whether or not it is merely a quirk of the fixture list, this midweek features superpower summits, games between arguably the four likeliest sides to win the competition – though Real Madrid may disagree with that – in Paris Saint-Germain against Barcelona and Bayern hosting Arsenal.

Arsenal can look like the anomaly among them. Each of the other three can make a case to have the best attack on the continent. Bayern's is supported by the statistics. Last season, they got a record 122 Bundesliga goals, bettered only by the Torino team of 1947-48 in a top-five European league. It was 51 more than Arsenal scored in winning the Premier League. In all competitions, Harry Kane got 61 himself. In all, Michael Olise got 22 goals and 28 assists.

Arsenal are spared the test of how to halt Olise; he stopped himself with his silly sending-off against Viking last week, and is suspended now. But the sense that these sides were playing very different versions of the same sport was underlined in May's Champions League semi-finals.

Bayern went to the Parc des Princes and, with Paris Saint-Germain, contributed to a classic. There were still 20 minutes remaining when the score stood at 5-4. Fantasy football, perhaps, or a dereliction of duty in defending, in the eyes of some. Meanwhile, Arsenal found a more prosaic way of progressing to the final, drawing 1-1 away with Atletico Madrid and winning 1-0 at the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta's way took him a round further than Vincent Kompany, even if both ended up exiting the Champions League at the hands of PSG. But that, in turn, was a consequence of the draw that stemmed from a shared excellence in the initial phase of the competition. Arsenal and Bayern were on opposite sides of the draw after finishing first and second in the group stage. Between them, they won 15 of 16 games, denied only a clean sweep by meeting each other: Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates last November.

That victory – with eight shots on target and an xG of 2.72 – could be seen as a sign Arsenal can create and score against the best. It is nevertheless the case that they look to have less firepower than they did in the Champions League final. Chief executive Richard Garlick spoke in the summer about wanting to bring in players who "change the dial". Yet possible dial-changers like Vinicius Junior, Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers eluded them.

The only attacking addition, Christos Tzolis, is injured now. More forwards went out than in during the summer and one of those, Gabriel Martinelli, completed the scoring against Bayern last year. Another of the scorers that day, Noni Madueke, got the only goal against Forest; Eberechi Eze, who made way for Madueke at the break, struck against Lille last week. Yet while Arteta's stand-in left wingers have scored, it still feels a problem position, and the one where they least look Champions League winners.

The questions facing Bayern swirl more around the defence. A former defender has been struggling: a virus meant Kompany had to miss Tuesday's training session and sit out the pre-match press conference. Meanwhile, Manuel Neuer is a doubt and Jonas Urbig could deputise in goal.

Bayern and Arsenal can differ in other respects. The German champions brought in Ismael Saibari, who could stand in for Olise, and Nathaniel Brown this summer, but Arteta's squad is constructed with a far greater emphasis on depth, on covering every base. If Arsenal have relative few goals of late, substitutes have scored in their last three games.

That is part of Arteta's model: clean sheets, consistency, quality options. Bayern's is based more around formidable firepower. After 184 goals last season, they already have 36 this season. Their strategy may be more entertaining, and if it is oversimplifying to call it attack versus defence when perhaps each is looking for a balance that involves playing to their strengths, it is a 90-minute examination of contrasting blueprints to win the Champions League.

Declan Rice of Arsenal is challenged by Harry Kane and Michael Olise in last season's Champions League (Getty)

articles.title: Raphinha sends defiant message after Barcelona defeat to PSG ahead of El Clasico: ‘It was a good test and shows we can compete’
articles.summary: Barcelona captain Raphinha has insisted that his side’s 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain will not affect their preparations for El Clasico, backing the team...
articles.body:
Barcelona captain Raphinha has insisted that his side's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain will not affect their preparations for El Clasico, backing the team's performance despite losing their first match of the 2026/27 season.

Returning to the starting lineup against the reigning European champions, the Brazilian forward acknowledged the difficulty of playing PSG on their home ground but argued that Barcelona had demonstrated their ability to compete.

With Real Madrid next on the schedule, Raphinha also provided an update on his own fitness and addressed the uncertainty surrounding Dani Olmo's condition.

Raphinha recognised the challenge Barcelona faced against Luis Enrique's side, highlighting the quality of their opponents and the difficulty of playing in front of their supporters.

"We knew it could happen; we're facing the two-time European champions, and playing in front of their fans is very tough."

Although disappointed not to take anything from the contest, the Barcelona captain played down the significance of losing three points, stressing that the team must learn from the experience rather than dwell on the result.

"We wanted to come away with a win or a point – whatever – but it's no big deal; these things happen when they're meant to, and in the end we've only dropped three points."

Raphinha also praised the tactical quality of PSG, believing Barcelona's ability to compete in possession provided encouragement despite the scoreline.

Raphinha returned to the starting XI against PSG. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images)

"They are a very well-drilled side. Despite today's result, we competed well. Both teams like to play with the ball and we had possession.

"It was a good test and shows we can compete. The result doesn't matter, but we played well."

Barcelona captain explains fitness plan after return

The PSG fixture marked Raphinha's return to the starting XI, but his involvement was carefully managed following a limited period of training.

"After all, I've had less than a week's training, and this was the plan – to play fewer minutes."

The forward was nevertheless encouraged by how he felt after the match, suggesting that his physical condition is moving in the right direction as Barcelona approach a crucial domestic fixture.

"I finished the match feeling good and strong, and I'm trying to improve my physical condition further."

His return is an important development for Hansi Flick, although the planned restriction on his minutes indicates that Barcelona are continuing to manage his workload.

Raphinha is confident ahead of El Clasico. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Raphinha also admitted that he did not yet know the details of Dani Olmo's injury after the midfielder was forced off against PSG.

"I don't know what happened to Dani, and now we'll speak to the manager and the doctor to find out what happened."

Raphinha insists PSG loss will not affect El Clasico

Barcelona will now turn their attention to Sunday's meeting with Real Madrid, with Raphinha eager to ensure that the European setback does not carry over into El Clasico.

The captain said the team would listen to Flick's assessment and work on the areas requiring improvement before the next match.

"We'll see what the manager has to say about how we can improve and be in good shape for the Clasico."

Asked directly whether the defeat could influence Barcelona's preparations or mentality ahead of facing their biggest rivals, Raphinha simply said

"It can't affect it at all," he concluded.

articles.title: Real Madrid superstar leaves Mourinho and teammates stunned with incredible work ethic
articles.summary: Real Madrid have completed 100 days under Jose Mourinho since the charismatic manager’s return in the summer.The team may have had a mixed bag of performance...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have completed 100 days under Jose Mourinho since the charismatic manager's return in the summer.

The team may have had a mixed bag of performances, but their record at home in particular has been exceptional.

Now, according to El Chiringuito TV (h/t Madrid Xtra ), Jude Bellingham is making a remarkable impression behind the scenes at Real Madrid.

The English midfielder, who is set to sign a new long-term deal with the club , is spending up to eight hours a day at the club's Valdebebas training complex.

Bellingham is consistently the last player to leave the training facilities, with his dedication surprising both his teammates and manager Jose Mourinho.

Bellingham setting an example at Valdebebas

The midfielder shows exceptional commitment to his daily routine. His work extends well beyond the usual first-team training sessions.

Spending up to eight hours at Valdebebas does not necessarily mean eight hours of physical training, but it does show Bellingham's commitment.

Bellingham is setting an example at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Nevertheless, the dedication offers an interesting insight into Bellingham's approach to maintaining his performance levels.

Mourinho is understood to be particularly impressed, while the midfielder's teammates have also taken notice.

For a player already established among Madrid's most important figures, such commitment sends a positive message throughout the dressing room.

Why Mourinho will value Bellingham's mentality

Bellingham's importance to Real Madrid extends beyond his technical ability and attacking contributions.

His willingness to work, compete physically and take responsibility in demanding situations makes him an important part of Mourinho's midfield.

The Portuguese manager has historically placed considerable emphasis on discipline, competitive mentality and players who put the team ahead of anyone else.

Mourinho will love to see Bellingham's attitude in the rest of his squad. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images)

Bellingham's training habits are well suited to those expectations. There is also a broader benefit for Madrid's developing squad.

With several new signings adapting to Mourinho's methods, having established players demonstrate strong professional standards will set an example.

However, workload management remains equally important, particularly during a season featuring domestic and European commitments.

Long hours at the training ground are valuable only when combined with appropriate recovery and carefully managed physical demands.

Bellingham is one of the first names on the team sheet for Jose Mourinho, and there is a good reason why this is the case.

It remains to be seen how the Englishman fares through the course of the season and whether his dedication influences the rest of the squad.

articles.title: La selección de Euskadi se medirá a Venezuela el 14N en San Mamés
articles.standfirst: El partido es uno de los actos de la conmemoración del 90 aniversario del Gobierno Vasco
articles.summary: El partido es uno de los actos de la conmemoración del 90 aniversario del Gobierno Vasco
articles.body: La selección de Euskadi recupera actividad y el 14 de noviembre se medirá a Venezuela en un amistoso que se disputará en San Mamés. La selección vasca contará con representación de todos los equipos profesionales vascos salvo el Eibar, que disputa la Segunda División y esa fecha tendrá competición al no parar el torneo durante las ventanas FIFA. La Federación Vasca resalta que "será uno de los primeros grandes momentos públicos de la nueva etapa de Euskal Selekzioa, con la unión como hilo conductor. El encuentro forma parte de los actos de celebración del 90 aniversario del primer Gobierno Vasco. La cita aspira a ser una celebración de las relaciones entre dos sociedades unidas por una larga historia de intercambios, migraciones, acogida y vínculos culturales.Dos pueblos unidos por historias que cruzan océanos. La historia compartida adquirió una nueva dimensión en el siglo XX, cuando Venezuela acogió a personas vascas que tuvieron que abandonar Euskadi durante la Guerra Civil y la posterior dictadura franquista. La diáspora contribuyó a mantener los vínculos con su tierra de origen y a fortalecer una relación que perdura hasta hoy". Los seleccionados entrenarán el viernes 13 en Lezama y quedarán concentrados antes del encuentro para volver a sus clubes el domingo 15. Todos los equipos han dado su conformidad a la disputa del encuentro y la Federación hace gestiones para que en la convocatoria estén futbolistas vascos de otros clubes distintos a los del territorio.

articles.title: Animal rights group Peta asks Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
articles.summary: Animal rights group Peta is urging Crystal Palace to retire their bald eagle mascot, saying a "bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals".
articles.body:
An animal rights group is urging Crystal Palace to retire their live bald eagle mascot with immediate effect, saying a "bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals".

In a letter to Palace CEO Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) asked the Premier League club to stop using the eagle, named Phoenix, in pre-match displays at Selhurst Park and to never use live animal mascots again.

The London team, known as the Eagles since 1973, introduced a live eagle to matchdays in 2010. Kayla, who died in 2020, performed the role for 10 years and her replacement Phoenix made her debut against West Ham in August 2024.

Peta says birds can become "frightened, disoriented and panicked" in stadium environments, putting themselves and fans at risk.

Using them for displays and entertainment also denies the animals, who "would naturally avoid humans", the opportunity to engage with their natural instincts, leading to "frustration and stress", the group said.

The organisation has "detailed records" of incidents involving live mascots, including birds, being injured or killed in collisions with walls, windows and match balls, as well as a falcon embedding its talons in a spectator's scalp after landing on his head.

In 2017, a Charlton Athletic fan was found guilty of trying to punch Kayla the eagle at a League Cup fixture two years earlier.

"Many professional sports teams use only willing humans as mascots and the club already has Pete the Eagle to excite the crowd," said Dr Carys Bennett, Peta's senior corporate projects manager.

"Bald eagles are widely recognised as symbols of freedom. They deserve better than to be used as an entertainment prop to amuse the Eagles' fans."

articles.title: Michael Carrick rejects Erik Ten Hag claim over ‘toxic culture’ at Man United
articles.summary: Manchester United have failed to win any of their last six matches
articles.body:
Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick insists he retains the support of the Manchester United board as he takes his depleted side to Como searching for a much-needed Champions League victory.

Pressure continues to mount on the former midfielder following United's poorest start to a league season in 40 years, with just two wins from 10 matches in all competitions.

The Red Devils enter Wednesday's clash against Cesc Fabregas' side without a win in six matches, following pre-match focus on comments from former boss Erik ten Hag.

In an interview with The Athletic two years after his dismissal, the Dutchman accused the club of broken promises, though Carrick claims he has no position concerns.

"I don't need any reassurance," the United head coach said. "It's pretty clear. I know the role, I know my responsibilities. I don't need anyone else to tell me that or tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better. I know that myself.

"I know the realities and I've got no problem with that. It's pretty clear. There's not much I can really elaborate on that. I know we've got to win football games for everything to flow and everything to fit into place. That's the great thing about it. We can do something about it.

"Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give. We've had some good performances. We've had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We've made some mistakes.

"But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there's a lot of togetherness there. There's a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important."

Asked if he feels backed, the United boss said: "Yeah. Why wouldn't I? I'm in this position, I have a good relationship – a really good relationship with everybody at the football club.

"There's really no issues and no problems with any of that side. We've got to win games of football and that's what we're striving to do."

Ten Hag had said that Man United "are continuing the toxic culture. They fuel it, they give the power to the players. Rashford is an amazing player, if his mindset is right. I always showed my trust in him, played him. But when you show these standards, sometimes you have to make corrections."

Without a win since beating Sabah 4-0 in September's Champions League opener, Carrick's hopes of halting that run against an improving Como side face major selection issues.

Eight squad members are sidelined through illness or injury, while Leny Yoro is suspended following his red card in last week's 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid.

"Bit of a mixed bag, to be honest," Carrick said. "We have quite a few who are missing. Licha (Lisandro Martinez) is not too bad, but he is not with us. We will have to see if he's ready for the weekend (against Bournemouth) or not.

"Kobbie (Mainoo) we're probably maybe looking at another 10 days or so but not exact. Luke (Shaw) a little bit longer than that.

"Ayden (Heaven) is ill and Marcus (Rashford) is still feeling a little bit of a hip issue that we are trying to overcome. Hopefully that'll be soon as well."

Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte are also injured for United, who were greeted by steady rain on landing in Italy on Tuesday evening.

Over 6cm of rain is forecast in the 24 hours before kick-off, with an orange warning for "severe weather" issued by the Italian Air Force National Meteorological Service.

Asked if he had any concerns about the surface or even the match being impacted, United boss Carrick said: "No, nothing immediate for me. We're kind of used to the rain, so we'll make the most of it."

articles.title: The night Rio Ngumoha became a huge problem
articles.summary: Watch out Europe – the 18-year-old winger starred in Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win over Villarreal and took a sizeable step forward with his devastating talen...
articles.body:
If the nature of their rivalry with Brazil means many an Argentinian will not gush about Rio, Alexis Mac Allister was a happy exception. "Rio was amazing," he said, and if he was talking about Rio Ngumoha rather than Rio de Janeiro, the sentiments were shared.

The Kop borrowed a chant from other historic enemies, Manchester United, to salute the 18-year-old as he became the youngest Liverpool player to assist a goal in the Champions League or to make two in a game since Michael Owen in 1998 . Which, to put it another way, was about a decade before his birth.

Liverpool's comeback win against Villarreal had the feel of another night when Ngumoha took a sizeable step forward. Although, given the speed at which he surged, his acceleration may have taken him further than that. Sometimes teenage talents have technique before they have the physique but it was notable how much speed and power Ngumoha showed on the burst to set up Mac Allister's second goal.

"The man came tight to me and the ball came, my first touch was direct and then I'm able to run at pace. Macca, good finish," said Ngumoha. Andoni Iraola was quick to point out that the winger could have gone down and perhaps got a penalty. The thought did not seem to enter Ngumoha's mind.

He likes running at defenders, but also getting past them. "Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one-v-one or two-v-one sometimes, by all means I'll do it," he added. "I believe in myself to do it."

Liverpool have believed in Ngumoha for a while, but also realised they had to show some patience. Arne Slot was booed when he took the youngster off against Chelsea in May but was always conscious of how many minutes to give a player adjusting to first-team football. There are other reasons why his introduction to the side has been gradual. "He struggled defensively in the first half," said Iraola on Tuesday. "The second half was much better." Mac Allister also pointed out the rookie's work off the ball.

Iraola added: "Today he didn't have an easy game also because they were demanding him defensively and their left-back was attacking a lot." Ngumoha was able to turn the tables and Iraola said: "There was a moment offensively where he was very difficult to stop. If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, he produces things. The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. Also, endurance-wise he is able to play more and more minutes. We were pushing him a little bit."

The sense is that Ngumoha is both a quick learner and a willing one. "I am very happy with his attitude because he tries to improve the things we think he needs to improve," said Iraola. "He is eager to add more things to his game."

One is the capacity to play on the right. The right winger who used to star on Merseyside on Champions League nights was Mohamed Salah. On Tuesday, it was Ngumoha. Yet after Liverpool missed out on the signing of Yan Diomande, they ended the transfer window with four wingers who prefer to play on the left. Since then, it has seemed they are taking it in turns to impress on their less-favoured flank. Cody Gakpo has delivered from terrific crosses from the right. Victor Munoz has scored one goal operating as a right winger and another as an auxiliary right-back. Ngumoha illuminated a Champions League night at Anfield when he was not even operating in his preferred position.

"He has changed the sides a lot. He has played a lot on the right," said Iraola, who wants wingers who he can use on either side. "Lately he is feeling so comfortable now and is having some shots with the left foot. He hasn't scored yet but he is getting there and if he adds small things to his game it will put him in an even better position."

Goalscoring is an area that offers scope for improvement. Ngumoha's tally stands at two goals in 39 games for Liverpool, even if only 15 were starts and he has only once completed 90 minutes. Liverpool's other three wingers have seven goals between them this season. He only has one since last August's 100th-minute winner at Newcastle .

"The good thing with Rio is he is still 18," Iraola said. "He is not the full package. He can add things, fortunately for us. Hopefully he can continue in the same way. He's not always going to be like this. He will have ups and downs in the process. But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place."

And Liverpool, lamentable in the first half-hour against Villarreal, triumphant by the end, were in a rather better place after he served Europe notice of his talent.

articles.title: Injury setbacks fuel Neill's hunger for Namibia tour
articles.summary: Ireland bowling all-rounder Jordan Neill feels past injury setbacks have made him "hungrier to come back harder" in the upcoming one-day series in Namibia.
articles.body:
Ireland bowling all-rounder Jordan Neill feels past injury setbacks have made him "hungrier to come back harder" in the upcoming one-day series in Namibia.

Neill has been selected by new head coach Gary Wilson for the five-match series that begins on Thursday in Windhoek (08:30 BST).

The 21-year-old made his Ireland debut at the age of 19 in 2025 but suffered a number of injuries following his Test debut series in Bangladesh, leaving him sidelined for the bulk of this year.

He has since returned to action and was drafted by the Amsterdam Flames in the inaugural European T20 Premier League and is now keen to make up for lost time.

"There were definitely times where I was a bit down in the dumps," South Africa-born Neill said of his injury setbacks.

"Coming back, it was almost like even more of a throwing into the deep end kind of thing because you've got to swim in Bangladesh. I think it's probably one of the hardest places to go as a fast bowler.

"I was very excited for the New Zealand Test at the beginning of the summer. I felt that, with having played the Bangladesh games, maybe I would have a shot to get in there for that match, so I really had the hopes up. But then I was hit with injury again and that was tough, especially being a Belfast boy."

Neill said he believes "everything happens for a reason", adding: "I think I'd also rather have that happen earlier on in my career than later on, learning to deal with injury and setback and it definitely does just make you a bit hungrier to come back harder."

Namibia tour good preparation for World Cup qualifier

Ireland's tour to Namibia will begin their preparations for next year's World Cup qualifier before the tournament is hosted by South Africa and Namibia.

Neill believes this series will give players the opportunity to stake their claim for a place in the squad and also help the team get up to speed in the 50-over format once more.

"With the World Cup coming up this time next year, and Namibia in particular co-hosting and especially with the need to qualify, it's definitely something that we're all pushing towards," he added.

"With the way things have gone with injuries to players this past six months, there have generally been a few spots up for grabs if guys put their hands up.

"This tour probably gives players an opportunity to try and get settled going into what would be the really important games coming up.

"Firstly, it's just great to get more 50-over cricket in, and then secondly, to try and balance out the side the way the coaches would want going forward."

articles.title: La 'luna de miel' que 'aleja' a Ronald Araujo del Barcelona: "Sin duda necesitaba ese cambio"
articles.standfirst: Sus goles y su buen rendimiento alimentan la opción de que el Liverpool ejecute su opción de compra
articles.summary: Sus goles y su buen rendimiento alimentan la opción de que el Liverpool ejecute su opción de compra
articles.body: "La opción de Ronald es una de esas que no existía en el mercado y de repente surgió la situación. Luego hablamos con el jugador y la primera conversación que tuvimos fue bastante alentadora. Se ve a un jugador ambicioso y experimentado que ha jugado en un club de primer nivel y está dispuesto a demostrar su valía", admite abiertamente Andoni Iraola. "A pesar de la atención que se presta a los fichajes millonarios del Liverpool, el jugador que consiguieron cedido del Barcelona se perfila cada vez más como una de sus operaciones más importantes", sugiere Aadam Patel en la 'BBC'. Estamos a finales de octubre, pero a orillas del Mersey cada vez se ve más viable que el 'Pool' pague la opción de compra que se guardó sobre el internacional uruguayo, valorada en 55 millones de euros. Y es que Araujo se ha convertido en 'titularísimo': acumula ya 11 partidos (692'), siete como lateral derecho -aprovechando las lesiones de Frimpong y Bradley- y cuatro como central. En Champions está viviendo su particular 'luna de miel'. Asistió a Dominik Szoboszlai en la victoria sobre el Atlético (2-1), marcó en la goleada sobre el LASK (3-6)... y volvió a 'mojar' en el triunfo sobre el Villarreal (4-3). Centró Rio Ngumoha desde la izquierda y el '33' del Liverpool aprovechó el despiste de Sergi Cardona para cabecear en boca de gol y poner el 2-2 en el añadido del primer tiempo. Araujo, por primera vez en su carrera, marcaba en dos partidos consecutivos de Champions. "Es uno de esos jugadores imprescindibles en cualquier equipo. Es alguien que lo da todo en el campo, que juega con pasión, que es un líder", aseguraba Stephen Warnock en la 'BBC'. "Ngumoha centra y Araujo lo hace muy bien: se arriesga y obtiene su recompensa metiendo el balón en el fondo de la red", apostilla Alan Shearer. Lo cierto es que el canterano del Barcelona ha caído de pie en Anfield. "Estoy feliz y mi familia también está muy feliz, eso es muy importante. Tengo muchas ganas de seguir adelante esta temporada, dar lo mejor de mí y continuar aprendiendo y creciendo como jugador", asegura Araujo. El uruguayo, sin embargo, prefiere evitar los debates sobre su futuro: "Es muy pronto para hablar de estas cosas. Estoy teniendo minutos de juego, que es lo que quiero y luego veremos qué pasa en el futuro". "Simplemente intento disfrutar cada día, seguir progresando, jugar y dar lo que se me exige para tener confianza", insiste Araujo, que valoraba positivamente en la 'Ser' su cambio a Inglaterra: "Sin duda necesitaba este cambio. Lo tenía muy claro, cuando terminó la temporada y nos fuimos al Mundial, era una decisión que tuve muy clara. Hablé con el club, con Deco, con el míster y ellos me lo hicieron muy fácil. Me ayudaron mucho. Creo que aquí estoy encontrando lo que necesitaba, que era jugar, sentirme importante y mostrar mi fútbol".

articles.title: VAR official Matt Donohue set for Premier League return after wrongly awarding Erling Haaland winner vs Man Utd
articles.summary: VAR Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus wrongly awarded Erling Haaland's winner for Man City against Man Utd in September; Enzo Fernandez was offside and interfering with play; Pro Ref apologised to Man Utd over mistake; Donohue has been refereeing in EFL
articles.body:
Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus failed to judge that Manchester City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was offside and interfering with play during the incident at Old Trafford on September 13.

Donohue is set to return to the Premier League and will serve as assistant VAR when Coventry host Fulham on Saturday.

He has not featured in any of the three match rounds since the incident, while Antrobus made his first appearance since the derby as an assistant referee for Newcastle's home fixture against Aston Villa last Saturday.

Donohue has officiated in the EFL since the derby, refereeing Championship matches between Derby and Wrexham on October 10 and Southampton vs Bolton last weekend.

Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb said Donohue developed "tunnel vision" by focusing on whether Haaland was offside, and added that the team around him should have helped pull him out of it. Sky Sports News reported United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision.

In the 59th minute, Haaland tapped in a cross to give 10-man Man City the lead, but the goal was ruled out on-field after the assistant referee signalled for offside on the striker.

The semi-automated offside technology ruled Haaland onside, so the goal stood, but City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was clearly offside when he dived to reach the same cross.

Although he didn't touch the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to affect Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez's defending before Haaland's back-post finish, which, under the laws of the game, should have meant the goal was disallowed.

In their post on X explaining why the goal was awarded, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

"The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

However, in a statement released hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref said it had contacted Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Haaland's winner.

A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

On Match Officials Mic'd Up , Webb said he was "really disappointed" by the decision and added: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

"The VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he is onside but when he runs it through the full APP (attacking possession phase), he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez.

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision but it is down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel but unfortunately, that did not happen on this occasion. This goal should have been disallowed."

What the officials said at Old Trafford...

Assistant referee: " I'm going to go offside, Haaland."

Referee: "On-field decision is offside."

VAR: " Checking the on-field decision of offside against Haaland. He's tight. He's onside, so now we need to check the full attacking possession phase (APP).

"Haaland's in an onside position, but I need to check the full APP. Go back to see if [Iliman] Ndiaye is onside when it is flicked. Yes. Go, go, go, so it should be a goal.

"No touch there [from Enzo Fernandez], confirm no touch. Clear gap. It's not a touch there, is it? Goal.

"Michael, confirming that you need to change your decision to goal. Haaland is in an onside position. Final decision is goal; check complete."

Sky Sports' Gary Neville predicted Pro Ref would issue a public apology for the mistake, but their statement fell short. He said: "We will see an apology from Pro Ref. There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off.

"It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong."

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher: "It's a bad one. We all look at it and it looks offside. Haaland looks offside but we know he's not. Then when you break it down, it is poor from the officials.

"It seems to me they've become obsessed with Haaland being onside. They haven't gone into as much detail with Fernandez in the middle and understanding of his impact on it."

Sky Sports' Micah Richards: "One hundred per cent [Fernandez is interfering]. It's been a bad day for referees and VAR.

"They got the Phil Foden decision wrong , and they got this decision wrong. How can you not say Enzo Fernandez is challenging for the ball? Of course he is.

"I've been in that position as a defender where any slight movement can make the difference for going for the ball or not, so of course it affects him. They've got it so wrong."

Sky Sports' Roy Keane: "Fernandez is interfering with play. Basically, United have been punished for holding a good line. When you are in that position, you are impacting the game. You're in the middle of the box, you're going for the ball.

"Their line is good. Fernandez is offside, and he goes to play the ball, so United are getting punished for good defending."

articles.title: Barcelona condemn PSG tifo inciting 'violence and hatred'
articles.summary: Barcelona report Paris Saint-Germain to Uefa after a tifo featuring a message which they say "incites violence and hatred in sport" was displayed ahead of Tuesday's Champions League match.
articles.body:
Barcelona have reported Paris St-Germain to Uefa after a tifo featuring a message which they say "incites violence and hatred in sport" was displayed ahead of Tuesday's Champions League match.

Ahead of kick-off at Parc des Princes, PSG fans behind one of the goals unveiled a banner featuring a masked figure in a PSG shirt destroying the Barcelona badge with a chainsaw.

Underneath the image, in French, were the words "massacre, Parisian style".

Banners featuring explicit messages were also on display during the match, with Barcelona "strongly" condemning the actions of PSG's supporters.

Barcelona lost 4-2 in the French capital after previously winning their opening two Champions League matches.

In a statement, Barcelona told BBC Sport: "The club strongly condemns the incidents that took place when the tifo was displayed in the stands, including the images of a blood-covered chainsaw attacking the Barca crest.

"These images were deeply disturbing and conveyed a message that incites violence and hatred in sport.

"We consider this kind of imagery and language unacceptable as it goes against the values of respect, fair play and sportsmanship that should be upheld in football.

"We believe that football should be a space for healthy rivalry, mutual respect, and passion for the game, free from messages that promoted hatred or violence."

Under article 16 of Uefa's disciplinary regulations, the "use of gestures, words, objects, or any other means to transmit a provocative message that is not fit for a sports event" can result in disciplinary measures, including a fine of 10,000 euros (£8,381) for a first offence.

BBC Sport has contacted Uefa and PSG for comment.
